newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RESULTS TODAY - POLIFIN SEEN LIFTING AECI.
newsitem.headline: RESULTS TODAY - POLIFIN SEEN LIFTING AECI.

text.p: South African chemicals firm AECI Ltd is set to post a healthy rise in profit, benefitting from a strong profit rise in joint venture operation Polifin Ltd and a good export performance, analysts said.
But they said that AECI would be weighed down by some of its other operations.
Earnings per share were seen on a range of 92.0 cents to 113.0 from 79.0 last time. The dividend was seen edging up to a range of 29.0 cents to 32.0, from 25.0.

Consensus figures for the results were for earnings of 103.4 cents and a dividend of 30.3, but analysts warned the firm was coming off a low base last year so exaggerating the size of the profit rise.
Polifin, in which AECI owns a 40 percent stake, last week reported a 19.0 percent rise in year earnings to 99.0 cents per share.
Analysts said AECI's Dulux paint operations were struggling in a market hit by the general malaise in South Africa's building and construction industry.
A routine ammonia plant shut-down at AECI's Kynoch unit had also hit problems and analysts suspect it may have cost more than the firm had budgetted for.

Another area of concern is the contribution from yarn business South African Nylon Spinners, which is facing pressure from a prices squeeze. "They are barely recovering cash costs (at SANS). I would love to see AECI get out of the business," one analyst said.
However, some analysts said AECI was addressing its problems and there were signs of a turnaround in Dulux and SANS. One analyst rated the stock a buy as a recovery play.
"I think there is going to be a good story here," he said.
